assessments.closureRisk: Low-moderate: the experiment is well-scoped and closable, but a weak variant design could yield a no-op result that doesn't discriminate.
assessments.dominantCost: Designing genuinely non-trivial encounter variants and re-running the full causal-episode probe suite across them; risk of shallow variant design.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Create 2-3 materially different bounded encounter variants, re-run causal-episode probes across all variants, and separate surviving priors from fixed-encounter overfit before any generalization claim.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: AF002 priors are partly fixed-encounter overfit; the causal-episode probe surface is the local discriminator that will split surviving vs. overfit priors under perturbation.

assessments.closureRisk: Low: gates are well-defined, but the outcome is binary pass/fail on already-selected mechanisms.
assessments.dominantCost: Mechanical acceptance and release overhead; low evidence-generation value.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Run final portable and physical gates, commit exact P5 source if gates pass, graduate via structured self-release.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Mechanism selection is largely complete; the remaining surface is a local acceptance/gate/self-release path with low frontier-changing potential.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Remaining work is closure activity, not frontier-changing evidence; it does not earn a new capability or narrow/generalize a prior.

assessments.closureRisk: Moderate: the audit may conclude no narrower surface is justified, yielding a no-op.
assessments.dominantCost: Dependency-graph audit and potential packaging build; value is conditional on a measurable cost reduction being found.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Audit Host import/dependency graph first; only build the smallest packaging candidate if a measurable cost reduction is found; dogfood against World and another non-MCP consumer.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: The 44 passing World tests suggest semantic compatibility is settled; the unresolved surface is packaging/import-graph cost, which may reduce to a local packaging defect or may be a distributed dependency-graph issue.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Value is conditional on a measurable packaging win; less direct frontier value than G-AF3's generalization experiment.

assessments.closureRisk: High: externally blocked; cannot close until DNS recovers.
assessments.dominantCost: External DNS blocker; no budget allocation can unblock the live experiments.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Retry no-tool incremental after DNS recovery; run no-tool replay/batch and resolved-provider controls; compare utilization and decision quality.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: The control-path repair is already causally admitted in the owner candidate source; the live experiments are externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery, not on any open research question.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Externally blocked on DNS recovery; budget cannot change the blocker, so it should be deferred.

assessments.closureRisk: High: fully blocked on nonexistent external resource; cannot close.
assessments.dominantCost: External authority/resource acquisition (independent host) that no research budget can provide.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Obtain independent Linux/systemd host, verify immutable deployment kit, provision disabled-first with separated signers and executor-only Trade credential.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Negative control: the dominant admission blocker is the absence of an independently administered Linux/systemd host; the WSL/Windows workstation cannot satisfy high-assurance separation regardless of budget.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Negative control; the required authority/resource does not exist, so it must be deferred per the admission prior.

result.choiceRationale: G-AF3 is the only candidate whose next unit of budget directly earns a frontier value that no other candidate can: prior-generalization / defect-discovery across materially different encounter variants. AF002 is complete and the current Genesis has almost no real environment variation, so robustness/generalization claims are not yet earned — this is a clear, closable experiment with a well-defined discriminator (which AF002 priors survive perturbations). R-P5 is close to closure but its remaining work is mostly mechanical acceptance/gates/self-release, which is activity rather than frontier-changing evidence. HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit with only conditional value (build smallest candidate only if measurable). H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery and should be deferred. F-C2-BLOCKED is the negative control: its dominant blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) does not exist, so it must be deferred regardless of importance.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether materially different Scenario/Genesis encounter variants cause AF002 priors to split into surviving vs. overfit subsets, revealing which robustness/generalization claims are actually earned.
result.selectionFalsifier: If the encounter variants turn out to be trivially equivalent (no real topology/position/resource/target perturbation), or if the causal-episode probes cannot be re-run across variants due to an unanticipated environment dependency, then G-AF3's frontier delta collapses to no-op and R-P5's mechanical closure would have been the better use of budget.
